title: LiquidAion Neural Observatory
description:
Experimental research software that couples a frozen pretrained language model (Qwen3-0.6B) bidirectionally to a sparse recurrent rate network whose connectivity is a 512-neuron subset of the adult Drosophila melanogaster connectome (FlyWire FAFB, materialization 783). Hidden states observed at decoder layer 6 drive the network. The network's state is decoded into a residual intervention at layer 14, and the modified activations feed back into the network. A PySide6 desktop observatory shows an unmodified (Clean) and a coupled (Fly) conversation next to the network's activity, drawn on registered FlyWire anatomy.

The release includes controlled same-prefix experiments (coupling, a random-topology control, and persistent versus reset state), session recording and offline replay, context-isolation regression tests, and an attractor diagnostic. The measurements show a reproducible causal pathway. They do not show cognition, a biologically faithful simulation, or an advantage of the biological topology over the random control.

Licensing: the original source code is MIT. The bundled FlyWire-derived data are CC BY-NC 4.0 (FlyWire Consortium; Dorkenwald et al. 2024, Schlegel et al. 2024). The bundled navis-flybrains meshes are GPL-3.0. Qwen3 weights are not included (Apache-2.0, downloaded separately).
notes: Experimental research software, not a peer-reviewed publication. FlyWire data: https://flywire.ai/guidelines. Tested on Linux with an NVIDIA RTX 3070 Ti (PyTorch 2.8.0+cu128).
